summary.value: Skeleton is used to represent a draft of page while the content loads.

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: When prefers-reduced-motion is set to reduce, skeleton still animates (at a slower 1.6s duration) rather than disabling the animation, since it is not decorative.
value.quote: When the user has prefers-reduced-motion set to reduce , the skeleton will use a 1.6-second animation. The animation is not decorative, so we do not disable it.

value.rule: The skeleton element should be marked aria-hidden="true" so it is hidden from assistive technology.
value.quote: Add the class name ds-skeleton to a <span> with aria-hidden="true" .

relations.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.note: Use spinner instead of skeleton when indicating the system is working on a task the user must wait for.
value.quote: Avoid skeleton when you need to indicate that the system is working on a task the user must wait for, use a spinner instead

value.note: Skeleton is an alternative to spinner for indicating loading, giving a preview of the content's eventual shape.
value.quote: Skeleton is an alternative to spinner when you want to indicate that content is loading.

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: Choose the skeleton variant based on the type of content being loaded, such as headings, text blocks or images.
value.quote: Choose the skeleton variant based on the type of content being loaded, such as headings, text blocks or images.

value.rule: Skeletons should mimic the structure of the actual content so the transition to the fully loaded content feels smooth.
value.quote: Try to mimic the structure of the actual content to make the transition to the fully loaded content feel smooth.
